Duration: 10 hours • Start: 8:40–9:30 a.m. • Languages: English and Spanish

Today you will travel from Mexico’s spiritual heart to one of the planet’s most impressive ancient cities. Your morning begins at the Shrine of Our Lady of Guadalupe, one of Latin America’s holiest pilgrimage sites. Exploring the extensive basilica complex, you will feel the deep devotion that fills the atmosphere. Visit the original sixteenth-century chapel and the striking modern basilica, which attracts millions of visitors each year.

Then step back in time at Teotihuacan, the legendary “City of the Gods.” Walk

along the Avenue of the Dead, stand beneath the towering Pyramids of the Sun and

Moon, and imagine life in this powerful metropolis that flourished long before the Aztecs. With insights from your experienced guide, the stones come to life with stories of cosmic connections, mighty rulers and enduring mysteries. After this unforgettable day, return to your hotel to relax and reflect on your journey through time.

Tour highlights:

● Visit the Basilica of Guadalupe, a sacred site of profound spiritual significance.

● Discover the ancient city of Teotihuacan, one of the most important

pre-Hispanic settlements in Mesoamerica.

● Admire the colossal Pyramid of the Sun and Pyramid of the Moon.

● Learn about Teotihuacan’s cosmic symbolism, mythology and engineering.

● Enjoy expert storytelling from a certified bilingual guide.

● Comfortable round-trip transportation is included in the price.

Included: Shared transportation, certified bilingual guide, admission to Teotihuacan,

visit to the Basilica of Guadalupe.

Not included: Meals, drinks, tips, personal expenses.

Departure for Teotihuacan, approximately 60 km northeast of the capital.
Visit one of the most impressive archaeological complexes of the central highlands: Teotihuacan, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
You will see the Citadel, the Temple of Quetzalcoatl, the Avenue of the Dead, the Pyramids of the Sun and Moon, the Palace of Quetzalpapálotl and the Temple of the Jaguar.
Do not miss the remarkable pre-Hispanic murals preserved in some of the less-visited parts of the archaeological complex.
Then depart for Tulpetlac and its shrine, associated with the apparition of Our Lady of Guadalupe to Juan Bernardino.
Return to Mexico City for a visit to the Plaza of Three Cultures and St. James Church.
Holy Mass.
